clue.text: Insignificant little queens

blocks.note: a plain synonym of little
Queens (British Queens) is a popular Irish potato variety, so queens are an example of these vegetables

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about some minor royals who don't count for much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queens' looks royal, but it is a variety of potato, much grown in Ireland. The plural is fair because the answer's second word is plural too.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for trivial matters of no importance describes things too unimportant to bother about, exactly what an insignificant thing is.

clue.text: Market now unsettled — a sign of slowdown ahead?

indicators.note: something unsettled has been disturbed out of its order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A financial commentator warns that the jittery market signals an economic slowdown.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about the economy; the definition is a road sign telling drivers to slow down for workers ahead. The question mark marks the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadworks warning signs reading this tell motorists to reduce speed because labourers are on the carriageway ahead.

clue.text: Girl, in middle of deluge, facing death

indicators.note: the middle of a six-letter word is its central pair of letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the two central letters of the word deluge
the US intelligence agency; the clue's words do not obviously give these letters

explanation.surface: A young woman caught in a flood faces the prospect of dying.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is LU plus CIA, but 'facing death' does not clearly give CIA: perhaps 'facing' sets the agency beside LU and 'death' alludes to the agency's deadly work. The parse is uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucia is a female first name, the Italian and Spanish form of Lucy, so it names a girl.

clue.text: Issue you start following for information

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so just that one letter is taken
coming after the other pieces, so this letter is placed at the end

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, for
gen is British slang for information
first letter of you

explanation.surface: A note about a publication issue that you begin reading for its information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a magazine edition, but it means offspring. GEN is British informal for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the legal and old sense means children or descendants, which is what progeny means.

clue.text: Sat up on row that's more appealing

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Someone sat higher up in a row of seats that offered a better view.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastier literally means having better flavour, and is used loosely for anything more attractive or enticing.

clue.text: Government's financial plan shows huge debt worked out over time

indicators.note: something worked out has been reshaped or solved, so these letters are rearranged
in a down entry, a piece placed over another sits above it, here at the bottom of the reworked letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A Treasury plan reveals how an enormous national debt will be repaid over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as 'across a period', but it places the time abbreviation after the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the Chancellor's annual statement of taxation and spending is known simply as this, the state's financial plan.

clue.text: Delight with return of online story?

indicators.note: something on its return comes back the way it went, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: E- is the prefix for electronic, as in e-mail
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A writer is pleased when their online story is well received on its return.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate someone is to fill them with joy or high spirits, a verb synonym of delight.

clue.text: Military order bridge as a concentration measure

blocks.note: the parade-ground command to stand to attention
a span is the stretch of a bridge, and to span is to bridge

explanation.surface: An army orders a bridge built as a measure to concentrate its forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concentration' suggests massing troops, keeping up the military picture, but it means mental focus.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names how long a person can keep their focus on a task, a gauge of mental focus over time.

clue.text: One who thinks PM is a waste of time

definitions.text: One who thinks PM is a waste of time

blocks.note: surface reading: the Prime Minister, scorned by a cynical voter

blocks.clueFragment: One who thinks PM is a waste of time
blocks.note: setter's reading: PM is post meridiem, the afternoon and evening, which someone at their best early in the day finds useless

explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, so the clue reads as a political grumble; it is really the hours after noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is lively and productive early in the day feels the later hours are wasted, so they dismiss the afternoon.

clue.text: Socrates wandering around north comes to where you are

indicators.note: something wandering does not stay on a fixed course, so the letters move about
the reworked letters go around the other piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: The philosopher Socrates strolls about to the north and arrives at your location.
explanation.walkthrough: A self-referential joke: the clue sits at the tenth across light, so the answer names the very place the solver is reading.
explanation.definitionFit: While solving this clue the reader is at that grid position, so the answer names exactly the reader's current spot.

clue.text: Her reaction regularly inspires poetry

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for 'one who inspires poetry', a noun

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A woman's response to something stirs a poet into writing verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, a goddess who gives poets their inspiration.

clue.text: Performer not given credit for producing more

blocks.note: first meaning: a film walk-on who is not named in the credits
second meaning: additional, over and above

explanation.surface: An uncredited actor complains about being asked to produce more work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Credit' looks financial, but it means the on-screen list of a film's cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A background film actor is called this, and as an adjective the same word means additional or further.

clue.text: One takes pleasure putting name on powerful waste chemical

indicators.note: putting one item on others places it after them, at the end

blocks.note: epic means grand or mighty
urea is the compound in which the body excretes nitrogen
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A chemist labels a potent waste product while someone else is enjoying themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An Epicurean follows Epicurus, devoting life to the enjoyment of fine food, drink and sensual delights.

clue.text: Unpleasant type displayed by outsides of every form of transport

indicators.note: the outsides of a word are its first and last letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: a troll is an ugly creature, or a nasty online provocateur
first and last letters of every

explanation.surface: A nasty character turns up on the outside of every kind of transport.
explanation.walkthrough: A trolley is a tram in some places and a cart in supermarkets and hospitals, so it counts as transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled cart for carrying goods, or in America a tram or streetcar, moves people or things from place to place.

clue.text: Invention Faraday let remain undeveloped

blocks.note: a lie is a made-up story, an invention
F is the symbol for the farad, the unit named after Michael Faraday
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: An invention of the scientist Michael Faraday was left to gather dust, never developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invention' and 'Faraday' suggest science history; the invention is a falsehood and Faraday is cut to his unit's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmland left unplanted for a season to rest is said to lie this way, so the idiom means stay unused.

clue.text: Left off opposition to being politically correct

indicators.note: each of the preceding words is replaced by its opposite

blocks.note: the opposite of left
the opposite of off

explanation.surface: A left-winger is excluded from opposing political correctness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left off' reads as 'omitted'; instead each word is swapped for its opposite. Right-on is British slang for fashionably liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal expression describes someone holding fashionably liberal or progressive views, close to being politically correct.

clue.text: Opera company starts to use new electronic signature music

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters, which are all that is kept

blocks.note: the Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera
first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An opera house starts using new electronic music as its signature sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The melody that announces a particular TV show or film each time is its signature piece of music.

clue.text: Koala fed endlessly, when getting mixed foliage

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the word is dropped
mixed things are jumbled together, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the word fed minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A koala being fed non-stop gets a varied diet of leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The koala's diet is eucalyptus, not oak, so the answer only half belongs in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf from an oak tree is a single piece of tree foliage, a particular example of it.

clue.text: Dive, or jump, into attack

indicators.note: one word goes into the other, so it is placed inside it

blocks.note: a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing
a leap is a jump

explanation.surface: A choice between plunging or leaping into an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dive' reads as a verb of plunging; it is a noun for a seedy venue. A fleapit is British slang for a shabby old cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is a disreputable, run-down place, and a fleapit is a dingy, scruffy cinema or theatre of that kind.

clue.text: City created by an idiot

blocks.note: taken as written
a twerp is a silly person

explanation.surface: A town said to have been founded by a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major port in Flanders in northern Belgium, the country's second largest urban area.

clue.text: A motionless insect picked up flower

indicators.note: picked up as a sound is heard, so the words are taken by how they are spoken

blocks.note: a, plus still for motionless, plus bee for the insect, said together

explanation.surface: Someone gathered up a dead-still bug from the garden and a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' and 'flower' suggest gardening, but the first signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Astilbe is a garden perennial with feathery plumes of tiny blossoms, so it is a kind of flowering plant.

clue.text: Dispatched a crowd inside to get confirmation, perhaps

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, enclosed by it

blocks.note: dispatched means sent
taken as written
to crowd is to cram together

explanation.surface: A crowd is sent indoors so that something can be confirmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confirmation' looks like verification; it is the Christian rite, hence 'perhaps' for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Confirmation is one of the Christian rites of the church, along with baptism and communion, so it is an example.

clue.text: Preserve queen as one delivering old-school punishment

blocks.note: to can food is to preserve it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal ordered to preserve the tradition of beating schoolchildren.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-school' is literal: caning was a punishment in schools of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who beats with a cane administers the corporal punishment once routine in British schools.

clue.text: Terrorist group, losing article belonging to them,  …

indicators.note: the group loses something, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A paramilitary organisation drops an item belonging to its members, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the next clue for the surface only; each has its own answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive determiner for a plural group marks something as owned by those people.

clue.text: Heading for championship?

blocks.note: first meaning: the caption at the top of a page or chapter
second meaning: the status of champion, as in a world boxing crown

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a team on its way to winning a cup; 'heading' is a noun for a caption.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the name printed atop a piece of writing and the status held by a sports champion.

clue.text: …  cancel yearly publication when second article goes missing

indicators.note: the article disappears, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: an annual is a book issued once a year
the indefinite article a, the second one in the word

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a yearly magazine is axed when a feature vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for the yearly book contains two As; 'second' picks the later one to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a marriage or contract is to declare it void, which is to cancel it formally.

clue.text: Soviet leaders built poor revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The heads of the USSR created a shabby uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' fits the Soviet theme so neatly that it hides its role as the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Politburo was the chief policy-making committee of the Communist Party of the USSR, its ruling elite.

clue.text: How the young impatiently question progress towards objective

definitions.text: How the young impatiently question progress towards objective

blocks.clueFragment: How the young impatiently question progress towards objective
blocks.note: surface reading: young staff chafing at a project's slow progress towards its goal
setter's reading: children in the back of a car on a journey, endlessly asking whether they have arrived

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like office-speak about targets; the objective is simply a holiday destination and the question is a car-trip refrain.
explanation.definitionFit: Children bored on a long car ride famously keep asking this, demanding to know if the journey has ended.
